_comment: Diverse CC-licensed bird audio for testing detection + spectrogram marker localization. Sources are directly curl-able (iNaturalist static CDN, Wikimedia Commons, BirdNET-Analyzer repo) — NOT xeno-canto, which is now behind an Anubis anti-bot wall. Audio binaries are gitignored; this manifest + fetch.sh are the reproducible record. Run fetch.sh from a machine with outbound network (the workshop box blocks it).

clips.notes: Los Altos resident species; baseline single-bird precise-placement case.

clips.attribution: (c) Jennifer Rycenga, iNaturalist (San Bruno Mountain, CA)
clips.notes: Transient, broadband calls — good frequency/vertical-position test.
Metallic repeated chips — the 'pin should hop to each chirp incl. the last' case.

clips.scenario: single bird, rapid trill (dense repeated notes)
clips.notes: Trill = notes too close to resolve individually — exercises the dense/approx path.

clips.attribution: BirdNET-Analyzer, K. Lisa Yang Center for Conservation Bioacoustics
clips.notes: Canonical BirdNET test soundscape (~120s, overlapping species) — the multi-bird disambiguation case, and ground-truthable against BirdNET's published output.
Many overlapping callers — stress test for simultaneous-bird differentiation + card crowding.
Non-local species — tests the range filter / false-positive handling AND a very busy heatmap.
